title: A set exported in the model's own chat shape, checked against its template (D2, P5)
request: For training a local Qwen on the M1 Max the owner wants every earlier turn of a training example to keep its thinking, built with the same template and setting as when the model runs (preserve_thinking), and tool arguments as objects, not text: 'if training and running use different templates, the model learns one habit and is used with another'.
spec: Plan D2 whole step record, package P5 (plans/yes-you-are-right-jaunty-parasol.md): export_chat (tools + messages, reasoning_content on recorded reasoning only, object arguments, tool_call_id, sealed never, silver refused, the manifest with the commit) and template_check (each line rendered with the tokenizer's template and the run-time kwargs; every reasoning and every tool call must survive).
plan: the export shape from the v2 contracts (ChatExample.tools, Message.tool_call_id, SolverTrajectory.tools)
export_chat: chat examples and trajectories as lines; silver refused by the manifest's consent; sealed never read
template_check: Jinja alone (no model library), the tokenizer folder's template, the run-time kwargs, a problem per turn
tests with a tiny template that keeps or drops earlier thinking

decisions.decision: reasoning_content only on turns whose reasoning_source is recorded
decisions.why: a visible thought, a rule's line or a teacher's text is not the model's thinking; exporting it as such would teach the model to think in replies

decisions.decision: A trajectory's user turn is the problem's request and kind only
decisions.why: the table's hash, the answerer and the session's status are the record's, not the model's prompt

decisions.decision: The template check needs Jinja only, reading chat_template.jinja or tokenizer_config.json
decisions.why: the check must run where transformers is not installed (.venv); the tokenizer folder is the owner's download

decisions.decision: tojson renders in the recorded key order with ensure_ascii off, as the model libraries' template filter does; the check accepts the recorded, the sorted and the compact form
decisions.why: the check must see the text the model is trained on; a template that sorts or compacts still renders the same object

decisions.decision: Silver is refused by the manifest's consent (improve), not by a flag
decisions.why: the manifest is the one place the rule lives; an export cannot forget it

change: dclab_rnd/store/export_chat.py (new), dclab_rnd/store/template_check.py (new), decisions/finetune/README.md (the two commands), tests/test_store_export_chat.py (new).

findings.defect: the export imported a git helper that is local to the conductor's environment function
findings.fix: the export's own _commit() through subprocess, None outside a checkout

findings.defect: the argument check had a false pass: its fallback accepted every argument key quoted anywhere in the rendered text, and the tools' schema in the system prompt quotes them all
findings.scenario: a template rendering arguments as a Python repr, with tools offered: no problem reported
findings.cause: a lenient fallback meant for templates with another key order
findings.fix: the arguments' JSON itself must be in the text, in the recorded or the sorted key order (compact too); no key fallback
findings.impact: the check could not catch what it exists to catch

findings.defect: a thought with blank lines around it was reported as dropped: Qwen's template strips them inside the think tags
findings.fix: the reasoning stripped before the test
findings.impact: false failures on common model output

findings.defect: tojson sorted the keys while the model libraries' filter keeps the recorded order: the check did not render the text the model is trained on
findings.scenario: two-key arguments rendered in two orders
findings.cause: a wrong claim in a decision
findings.fix: insertion order, non-ASCII kept; the record's decision corrected
findings.impact: self-consistent today, wrong against a real tokenizer

findings.defect: the Jinja environment was not sandboxed and lacked strftime_now: a downloaded template could reach Python internals, and a Llama-style template failed on every line
findings.fix: ImmutableSandboxedEnvironment as the model libraries use, strftime_now defined
findings.impact: an unsafe render of an untrusted file
findings.open: {% generation %} blocks are still unknown to the environment

findings.defect: the export said nothing when the set's files disagreed with its manifest, when lines called tools with no tools list, or how long its longest line was
findings.scenario: the real studio v1 set: a manifest saying four rows and no train file; both real exports with tools empty on every line
findings.fix: mismatch, lines_with_calls_but_no_tools and longest_line_chars in the export's report; a row whose split is not train or dev skipped with a reason
findings.impact: a training run on a set that teaches calling unseen tools, or cut by max_seq_length, with no warning
findings.open: the sets' own gap (P4 fills tools on exchanges; the intern's sessions keep no schemas yet)

findings.defect: a tool turn recorded without its call id got call_<message index>, never matching its assistant turn's call id
findings.scenario: every M4 example from from_exchange before P4
findings.cause: no link to the preceding turn
findings.fix: the preceding assistant turn's call ids, in order
findings.impact: wrong for templates that render ids

findings.defect: _commit reported another repository's commit when the package was installed inside one
findings.fix: the git toplevel must be this repository's root
findings.impact: a wrong commit in a manifest

findings.defect: the README said the stock MLX trainer masks all but the last message; it trains every token unless --mask-prompt is given, and then only the last message
findings.fix: the README says it precisely and cites the fine-tuning note; jinja2 declared in requirements/base.txt
findings.impact: a wrong loss mask in a training run

measurements.name: the export and template-check tests
measurements.next: the owner runs template_check on a real export with a Qwen tokenizer; the reasoning folders of P4 feed it
limits: no real tokenizer template was rendered: Qwen's own template is checked by the owner on the Mac

outcome: A set exports as chat JSONL in the model's own shape with the tools offered, recorded reasoning on every turn that has it, object arguments and tool ids, never a sealed row and never silver; the template check renders each line with the model's template and the run-time setting and names the turn whose thinking or call did not survive.
lessons: Export the training shape from the contract, then check it against the model's template before any training run.
risks: a template that renders tool arguments in a shape other than JSON (an XML-style template) fails the argument check; the check then needs that template's shape
an export made before P4 fills the reasoning folders has few recorded reasonings
